Canadian Court Releases MS Patient Krieger On Bail
Without His Having To Promise Not To Use Medical Marijuana.
"The judge said it's not illegal to try and change legislation."

(Marijuananews note: First, it is tragic that Canada would lock up a seriously ill person in an attempt to silence him. Second, it is ridiculous that the people of Calgary should have to read this kind of reporting.)

September 9, 1999

From The Calgary Sun
callet@sunpub.com

By Kevin Martin

GRANTED BAIL

But crusader won't give up drugs

Marijuana crusader Grant Kreiger was released on bail yesterday – despite his refusal to promise to stay off the weed.

Justice Patrick Sullivan rejected submissions by Crown prosecutor Scott Couper that Kreiger should remain locked up because he won't eschew his miracle drug.

"The court should exercise some caution ... given his obvious commitment to overturn the law," Couper told Sullivan.

But the judge said it's not illegal to try and change legislation.

"He can promise to overturn the laws all he wants, that's not a crime," said Sullivan.

Defence lawyer Adriano Iovinelli said his client, who suffers from multiple sclerosis, has agreed not to grow or distribute marijuana until he can take his cause before a jury.

But Iovinelli said his client will still need to have a daily fix of weed to relieve the pain of his illness.

(Marijuananews note: I know just how he feels! I need my daily fix of really crappy biased pseudo-journalism, or my metabolism drops. The Calgary papers are usually good for a rush.)

Kreiger, 45, faces five-drug related charges.
